newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher after Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher after Wall St rise.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Wednesday in active trading triggered by a record rise of U.S. stocks on Tuesday, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.43 percent, or 3.59 points, to 255.11 on all-share turnover of 126 million shekels against 90 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.44 percent higher at 265.67.

"Stocks rose today across the board led by a sharp rise in Maof shares. The market was looking for a reason to rise and today the trigger was the Dow's rise," said Daniella Finn, head of sales at Batucha Securites and Investments.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 179.01 points to 6,962.03 on Tuesday which was close to the Dow's biggest ever rise in a day in points terms.

"The market is strong and the trend is clear. Wall Street was the reason for today's rise but it could have been anything else. The market simply wants to rise," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.
The trader said that foreign investors were also active buying shares.

The most active shares were Israel Discount Bank, which gained 0.25 percent to 344 agorot on volume of 10.5 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 1.25 percent to 16,996 agorot on volume of 8.6 million shekels.

Koor Industries, the third most active share, rose 1.50 percent to 29,427 agorot on volume of 8.9 million shekels. The company said on Wednesday that its subsidiary Telrad Holdings had decided to buy a further $10 million of shares in its parent company.
Clal Israel, the main gainer on the Maof, surged 5.0 percent to 97.5 agorot. Traders said there was no evident reason for the sharp rise.
